text:
jerry: hi team 👋 bringing up the dev stack and redis keeps crashing in the compose logs with `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/dump.rdb'`. Using M1 Mac + Docker Desktop. Anyone seen this?

lucy: welcome! two quick things: 1) are you bind-mounting a host dir into /data? 2) do you also have a local redis server running on the host?

jerry: compose snippet: `- ./redis-data:/data` and I had `ports: - 6379:6379` because I wanted to connect from Host.

sam: mounting host dir on mac can hit Docker's gRPC-FUSE permission mapping. Named volume avoids it: `volumes: redisdata:` then `- redisdata:/data`. Also if your host redis is running, the port bind fails and sometimes the container retries and leaves partial files with root ownership causing permission denied on restart.

jerry: oof I do have brew redis running locally. I stopped it and restarted compose, but still got permission denied.

lucy: try `rm -rf redis-data && docker-compose down && docker-compose up` after stopping host redis. If you need host file persistence, create the dir and chown it: `mkdir redis-data && sudo chown -R 999:999 redis-data`. Redis in official image runs as user 100 (or sometimes root depending on image), so mapping ownership helps.

infra-bot: Tip: our `./dev` wrapper recommends named volumes for redis and postgres to avoid macfs issues. See dev/README line 42.

jerry: switched to a named volume and removed the port mapping (I can use `docker exec -it redis ...` for quick checks). Now redis starts cleanly. One more Q: any preferred pattern for `.env.local` to avoid ambient host env interfering (I had `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379` set previously)?

sam: set `REDIS_HOST=redis` and `REDIS_PORT=6379` in `.env.local` for compose dev, or use `REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0`. That forces TCP to the service name instead of localhost socket. We also recommend documenting this in the onboarding checklist if you hit it.

jerry: thanks all — filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/issues/93 with steps I took (stop host redis, switch to named volume, avoid host port mapping) so future new-hires won't stumble on this. :tada:
